messages.subject: ggtreeExtra error when running the examples
messages.subject_clean: ggtreeExtra error when running the examples
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

When I run ggtreeExtra examples (http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/ggtreeExtra/inst/doc/ggtreeExtra.html) using this code:

p5 <- p4 +
      new_scale_fill() +
      geom_fruit(
          data=dat1, # The abundance of dat1 will be mapped to x,
          geom=geom_bar,
          mapping=aes(y=ID, x=Abundance, fill=Location),
          pwidth=0.4,
          stat="identity",
          orientation="y", # the orientation of axis.
          axis.params=list(
                          axis="x", # add axis text of the layer.
                          text.angle=-45, # the text size of axis.
                          hjust=0  # adust the horizontal position of text of axis.
                      ),
          grid.params=list() # add the grid line of the external bar plot.
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(
          values=c("#F8766D", "#C49A00", "#53B400", "#00C094", "#00B6EB", "#A58AFF", "#FB61D7"),
          guide=guide_legend(keywidth=0.5, keyheight=0.5, order=6)
      ) +
      theme(#legend.position=c(0.96, 0.5), # the position of legend.
          legend.background=element_rect(fill=NA), # the background of legend.
          legend.title=element_text(size=7), # the title size of legend.
          legend.text=element_text(size=6), # the text size of legend.
          legend.spacing.y = unit(0.02, "cm")  # the distance of legends (y orientation).
      )
p5

I encountered the following error:

> Error in `[[<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, xid, value = integer(0)) :
>   replacement has 0 rows, data has 230
> In addition: Warning message:
> The following column names/name: Location, Length, Group, Abundance are/is the same to tree data, the tree data column names are
> : parent, node, branch.length, label, isTip, x, y, branch, angle, Location, Length, Group, Abundance, xmaxtmp.

I succeed in generating P1, P2, P3 and P4, but failed at P5, am I wrong at any steps?

Sincerely,

Dong

messages.subject: Re: ggtreeExtra error when running the examples
messages.subject_clean: ggtreeExtra error when running the examples
messages.body_plain:
I think your p2 is generate from p1 ( using %<+%).  But the vignette used `p` to generate `p2`.

you can remove the data, since the `dat1` has been added to data of plot by `%<+%`. and remove the *y* aesthetic.

```

p5 <- p4 +
         new_scale_fill() +

         geom_fruit(geom=geom_bar,
                              mapping=aes(x=Abundance, fill=Location),

                              pwidth=0.4,
                              stat="identity",
                              orientation="y",

                              axis.params=list(axis="x",text.angle=-45,hjust=0 ),
                              grid.params=list() ) +

         scale_fill_manual(
                 values=c("#F8766D", "#C49A00", "#53B400", "#00C094", "#00B6EB", "#A58AFF", "#FB61D7"),
                guide=guide_legend(keywidth=0.5, keyheight=0.5, order=6)) +

         theme(legend.background=element_rect(fill=NA),
                      legend.title=element_text(size=7),
                      legend.text=element_text(size=6),
                      legend.spacing.y = unit(0.02, "cm"))
```

PS: I suggest that it is better to use `geom_fruit(data=dataset)`， only if you know what information ggtree object has contained, you can use `%<+%` to display the external circular layer.

messages.subject: align gheatmap rows with internal nodes?
messages.subject_clean: align gheatmap rows with internal nodes?
messages.body_plain:
Hey all,

I am plotting data associated with a tree using ggtree and the gheatmap function. It is pretty straight forward to align the rows with tips (works perfectly if rownames and tiplabels match up) so that works perfectly fine.

Is it at all possible to align rows of a heatmap with internal nodes instead of tips? I would like to summarize rows and plot averages of them aligned to internal nodes (clades) instead of a seperate row for every row.

I have extensively search every post associated with this topic and couldn't find anything, some tips would be greatly apprechiated.

If it requires something else than gheatmap, that would also be fine. I couln't find any feasible function at all, so anything would be apprechiated.

Best,
Fabian

height <- height * diff(range(tree_view$data$y, na.rm = TRUE)) )
I would like to plot absolute values, is there a possibility to do that (e.g. with barplots or using different symbols of sizes relative to the absolute value or bubble plots, etc)?
I hope I explained the request sufficiently, please let me know if you need more clarification.
Kind regards,
Sebastian
